title: Humanoid robots: the actuator and precision-component chain
map_limitation: Supplier-side EDGAR full-text search cannot surface this chain: the gating suppliers are Japanese (6324.T, 6268.T, 6481.T), Chinese A-share (688017.SS, 002472.SZ, 002050.SZ) and German (SHA.DE) filers with no SEC filings, and the largest humanoid OEMs (Figure, Apptronik, Agility, Unitree, 1X) are private and name no suppliers publicly. The entire upstream therefore enters via research and the repricing-lag lane, not via disclosure. Two further gaps to state plainly: dexterous-hand and tactile-sensor supply is almost entirely private or pre-revenue, so that link is mapped from technical literature rather than order books; and Chinese reducer capacity announcements (Shuanghuan's 500k-unit Suzhou plant) are company statements, not audited output, so the 2026-2027 supply picture is directionally sourced and quantitatively soft.

links.name: Onboard compute & vision-language-action models
links.role: The policy layer that turns hardware into a general-purpose worker; dexterous manipulation needs large volumes of examples and real-world feedback, creating demand for teleoperation, synthetic data, tactile datasets and VLA systems, with tighter humanoid-foundation-model integration expected [Fraunhofer IPA / arXiv VLA survey literature, as of 2026-02].

bottleneck.note: Compute is purchasable and improving fast; this link is where the narrative sits but not where the physical constraint is.

evidence.claim: Figure AI's Helix is a vision-language-action model that unifies perception, language understanding, and learned control into a real-time policy layer running directly on a humanoid robot, trained on approximately 500 hours of teleoperated behavioral data.
evidence.source_name: Figure AI, "Helix: A Vision-Language-Action Model for Generalist Humanoid Control"

evidence.claim: Vision-language-action (VLA) models are established in the robotics research literature as a policy layer connecting vision-language understanding to embodied robot control; a survey of more than 80 published VLA models documents this as an active, fast-growing research area directly applicable to humanoid systems.
evidence.source_name: arXiv (Sapkota et al.), "Vision-Language-Action (VLA) Models: Concepts, Progress, Applications and Challenges"

evidence.claim: Helix's onboard System-1/System-2 architecture directly outputs continuous whole-upper-body control for Figure's own humanoid platform at 200Hz, so the VLA policy layer is what drives the OEM's robot rather than a standalone research artifact.
evidence.source_name: Figure AI, "Helix: A Vision-Language-Action Model for Generalist Humanoid Control"

links.name: Battery, power & thermal management
links.role: Runtime and duty cycle gate the labour-substitution case; platforms are converging on certified swappable battery systems and inductive charging, with battery life still described as limiting and unit prices of $20,000-$150,000 keeping humanoids out of most workplaces [Vicon / DataM Intelligence humanoid market reviews, as of 2026-07].

bottleneck.note: Cell supply is abundant and shared with EV; the humanoid-specific work is packaging, swap architecture and thermal, which is engineering rather than scarcity.

evidence.claim: Battery and power-management technology is named as a distinct growth driver in the humanoid robot market alongside declining component costs, in a dated industry market-sizing report.
evidence.source_name: DataM Intelligence, "Humanoid Robot Market Size, Share & Forecast Report"

evidence.claim: Figure's Figure 03 humanoid platform ships with certified high-power wireless/inductive charging (2kW through foot-mounted coils) rather than a plug, and its battery pack carries UN38.3 safety certification, a concrete instance of the certified swappable/inductive-charging convergence the chain describes.
evidence.source_name: Figure AI, "Introducing Figure 03"

evidence.claim: The wireless-charging and battery-certification system described is built directly into Figure's own OEM robot (Figure 03): the battery-thermal subsystem is a component integrated into the finished humanoid platform.
evidence.source_name: Figure AI, "Introducing Figure 03"

links.name: Encoders, force-torque & tactile sensors
links.role: Joint encoders close the control loop, while force-torque and fingertip tactile sensors are what turn a gripper into manipulation; tactilely enhanced hands detecting forces as small as 3g are what enable dexterous handling across object types, and this cluster is named a major investment target [Fraunhofer IPA humanoid hardware value chain, as of 2026-02].

bottleneck.note: Encoders are a mature supply base; high-resolution tactile skin is the immature part and is mostly private or pre-revenue.

evidence.claim: Humanoid makers such as Unitree integrate high-resolution encoders and force/torque sensors directly into joint actuator modules; frameless torque motors, reducers, and sensors together form the joint's control-loop stack.
evidence.source_name: TechBuzzChina, "Actuators & Motors: The Muscles of China's Robots"

evidence.claim: Encoders and force/torque sensors are described as integrated components inside the humanoid joint actuator module itself, alongside the torque motor and reducer, not a separate downstream part.
evidence.source_name: TechBuzzChina, "Actuators & Motors: The Muscles of China's Robots"

evidence.claim: Each five-finger dexterous hand is covered with thousands of tactile contact points and high-pixel electronic skin, a direct cost and design driver for dexterous-hand manufacturers, i.e. tactile sensing is built into the hand.
evidence.source_name: 36Kr, dexterous-hand degrees-of-freedom competition article

links.name: Precision gear-grinding machine tools
links.role: Planetary roller screws and harmonic reducers need high-precision grinding tools to mass-produce, and those tools are still dominated by a few European and Japanese makers; machine-tool availability can therefore cap component capacity expansion and the whole humanoid ramp trajectory [Roland Berger / 36Kr humanoid hardware analysis, as of 2026-05].

bottleneck.note: The bottleneck behind the bottleneck: the largest specialists (Kapp Niles, Reishauer) are private, so exposure is only partially listed.

evidence.claim: A Chinese reducer maker (Taoshi Intelligent Technology) had to design its own custom 7-axis, 5-linkage precision grinding machine and rebuild machine tools, lead-screw guide rails, and control systems from scratch because no existing processing equipment in the industry could manufacture its component, direct evidence that specialized grinding and machine-tool capability gates production.
evidence.source_name: 36Kr, Taoshi Intelligent Technology financing and capacity article

evidence.claim: Harmonic-drive flexspline components must be machined to single-digit-micron tolerances, named as one of the primary bottlenecks, alongside torque sensors and motor drive systems, preventing humanoid robots from scaling past pilot production lines.
evidence.source_name: WhyChips, "Humanoid Robot Mass Production: Key Component Gaps"

evidence.claim: Harmonic-drive flexspline components require single-digit-micron machining tolerance, i.e. harmonic-reducer production depends directly on precision machine-tool capability.
evidence.source_name: WhyChips, "Humanoid Robot Mass Production: Key Component Gaps"

evidence.claim: The same class of precision-reducer manufacturing bottleneck, custom grinding machinery required because none existed off the shelf, applies to cycloidal/toroidal-style reducer geometries; the cited maker is a toroidal-worm reducer specialist rather than a named cycloidal-RV-reducer maker, so this is a general rather than reducer-type-specific match.
evidence.source_name: 36Kr, Taoshi Intelligent Technology financing and capacity article

evidence.claim: The same precision manufacturer had to redesign machine tools, lead-screw guide rails, and control systems from scratch, i.e. lead/roller-screw-class linear components share the same custom machine-tool dependency.
evidence.source_name: 36Kr, Taoshi Intelligent Technology financing and capacity article

links.name: Planetary roller screws & linear guides
links.role: The linear actuation path used in legs and heavy-load joints; for linear motion the analogous choke points are roller screws and high-durability linear guides, where capacity and qualification cycles can be even more restrictive than in rotary reducers [McKinsey humanoid supply-chain analysis, as of 2026].

bottleneck.note: Qualification cycles, not raw capacity, are the stated constraint; a qualified line cannot be substituted quickly.

evidence.claim: Planetary roller screws convert rotary motor motion into precise linear actuation for high-load humanoid joints (used by Tesla Optimus, Figure, Agility, 1X); manufacturing demands specialized expertise and precision machinery with relatively few global suppliers, driving unit costs of $1,350-$2,700 and roughly one-third of total actuator manufacturing cost.
evidence.source_name: Humanoids Daily, "Planetary Roller Screws: The High-Stakes Component Powering Humanoid Robot Motion"

evidence.claim: Roller screws dominate payload-oriented leg actuation (knees, ankles) where load is high and stroke is short, with a specific precision-grinding operation identified as a critical manufacturing chokepoint controlling supplier access to this component category.
evidence.source_name: humanoid.guide, "The Humanoid Actuation Report"

evidence.claim: Roller screws are one of the primary transmission types, alongside harmonic, cycloidal, and quasi-direct-drive designs, packaged into the actuator, which as a whole carries 40-60% of a humanoid's bill of materials.
evidence.source_name: humanoid.guide, "The Humanoid Actuation Report"

links.name: Cycloidal / RV reducers
links.role: The higher-load rotary alternative used in hips, knees and industrial arms, and the relief valve on harmonic supply: Nabtesco is the global number one in RV reducers and is doubling capacity by 2026 for anticipated humanoid demand, with Zhejiang Shuanghuan bringing on a Suzhou plant described as 500,000 units of annual reducer capacity [KraneShares / humanoid.guide capacity reporting, as of 2026-04].

bottleneck.note: Less concentrated and further along in capacity expansion than harmonic, which is exactly why it matters: it caps how much pricing power the harmonic link can hold.

evidence.claim: Nabtesco launched new compact precision reduction-gear product lines (RVmini and Monocrank series) explicitly to address growing demand from collaborative and humanoid robot markets, building on cumulative production of over 14 million reduction-gear units.
evidence.source_name: Nabtesco Corporation, official news release

evidence.claim: Nabtesco is reported to be doubling its RV-reducer capacity by 2026 for anticipated humanoid demand, while Zhejiang Shuanghuan Driveline is bringing on a new Suzhou plant in 2026 described as adding 500,000 units of annual reducer capacity, supplying Optimus and Unitree.
evidence.source_name: Next Financial (Substack), "The Joint Problem: Who Owns the Most Expensive Part of a Humanoid Robot"

evidence.claim: Cycloidal and strain-wave-class reducers are paired with frameless torque motors as the dominant rotary actuator architecture in torque-critical humanoid joints, packaged together into the actuator module.
evidence.source_name: humanoid.guide, "The Humanoid Actuation Report"

links.name: Harmonic / strain-wave reducers
links.role: The compact high-ratio gearbox used at most humanoid rotary joints, and the link the signal names as the binding constraint: lead times run 26+ weeks and precision-manufacturing limits make it structurally harder to scale than electronics, with supply concentrated among Harmonic Drive Systems, Nabtesco and Chinese entrant Leaderdrive [Roland Berger / KraneShares humanoid research, as of 2026-05].

bottleneck.note: Tighter tolerances and a more concentrated supplier base than the cycloidal alternative; J.P. Morgan puts Leaderdrive at 30-40% of the Chinese harmonic market, and HDS guided FY2027/3 operating income up 141.5%.

evidence.claim: J.P. Morgan estimates Leaderdrive holds 30-40% of China's harmonic-reducer market; Leaderdrive's 2025 revenue rose 47% to 570.7 million yuan with net profit more than doubling on industrial-robot and humanoid demand, with customers including Agibot and UBTech.
evidence.source_name: humanoid.guide, "Leaderdrive: Harmonic Reducers Surge as Humanoid Demand Lifts Shares"

evidence.claim: Harmonic Drive Systems' own investor-relations guidance forecasts fiscal year 2027 (ending March 2027) consolidated net sales of 68.0 billion yen and operating profit of 6.2 billion yen, corroborating the reducer maker's guided growth, though the chain's specific +141.5% operating-income figure could not be independently reconciled from this page.
evidence.source_name: Harmonic Drive Systems, official IR "Financial Results Forecast" page (live page, accessed this run)

evidence.claim: Harmonic and strain-wave reducers combine with frameless torque motors as the dominant rotary joint-actuation architecture, packaged into the actuator module alongside drive electronics.
evidence.source_name: humanoid.guide, "The Humanoid Actuation Report"

links.name: NdFeB rare-earth magnets
links.role: High-energy-density neodymium magnets go into every joint motor; no commercially viable substitute offers comparable energy density at acceptable size, and China dominates midstream processing and magnet manufacturing, giving it leverage over the pace and cost curve of the whole build-out [Adamas Intelligence / Oceanwall rare-earth supply-chain research, as of 2025-10].

bottleneck.note: Named repeatedly as the material bottleneck behind humanoid mass production; concentration is geopolitical, not merely industrial, so export policy can gate volumes independent of demand.

evidence.claim: Neodymium-iron-boron (NdFeB) magnets are identified as vital components for humanoid robot joint motors, alongside EVs, wind turbines, and defense uses, with supply-chain security for this material named a central industry concern.
evidence.source_name: Adamas Intelligence, "Humanoid Robot Revolution: NdFeB Supply Chain Implications and Strategies"

evidence.claim: Each humanoid robot uses roughly 3.5-4 kg of high-performance NdFeB magnets, about twice the magnet content of an electric car, and there is no physical substitute that fits.
evidence.source_name: China Unread (Substack), "The Bottleneck in Humanoid Robotics"

evidence.claim: The cited magnet content (3.5-4kg per unit) is explicitly framed as going into the joint motors themselves, i.e. NdFeB magnets are a direct input material to the torque/BLDC motors, not a separate downstream product.
evidence.source_name: China Unread (Substack), "The Bottleneck in Humanoid Robotics"

links.name: Frameless torque & coreless motors
links.role: Frameless brushless DC motors dominate humanoid joints on efficiency and availability, with permanent-magnet synchronous motors offering smoother commutation at higher cost; Chinese suppliers are described as already leading in coreless motors alongside harmonic reducers [Fraunhofer IPA humanoid hardware value chain / UBTECH cost commentary, as of 2026-02].

bottleneck.note: Motor winding capacity is expandable; the constraint sits upstream in the magnet, not in the motor itself.

evidence.claim: Frameless torque motors are the dominant motor type in high-load humanoid joints (hips, knees, ankles) and represent about 16% of a typical humanoid's component cost (25% combined with coreless motors); Chinese suppliers (Inovance, Step Electric, Aoyi Technology, Moons' Industries) are ramping capacity and undercutting foreign coreless-motor prices by 40-70%.
evidence.source_name: TechBuzzChina, "Actuators & Motors: The Muscles of China's Robots"

evidence.claim: The humanoid joint module is described as a sealed module combining a frameless torque motor, precision reducer, torque sensor, dual encoder, and drive electronics, i.e. the torque motor is a named direct input into the packaged actuator module.
evidence.source_name: TechBuzzChina, "Actuators & Motors: The Muscles of China's Robots"

links.name: Integrated actuator modules
links.role: Where reducer, motor, encoder and drive electronics are packaged into the joint the OEM actually buys, and the layer incumbents are racing to own: Schaeffler signed three humanoid actuator partnerships in five months (Neura, Humanoid, Leju) co-developing next-generation strain-wave gear actuators, while Sanhua is flagged as a likely Optimus actuator supplier off its Tesla thermal relationship [KraneShares humanoid research, as of 2026-04].

bottleneck.note: The contested margin layer: whoever integrates the joint captures the reducer's scarcity rent or hands it to the OEM. Which way that resolves is the chain's central open question.

evidence.claim: Schaeffler signed three humanoid actuator partnerships in five months, with Neura Robotics, UK-based Humanoid, and China's Leju Robotics, co-developing next-generation strain-wave gear actuators, in an ecosystem where actuators comprise 40-60% of humanoid bill-of-materials and no dominant 'engine supplier' equivalent yet exists.
evidence.source_name: KraneShares, "Humanoid Robotics In 2026: The Race From Pilot To Platform"

evidence.claim: Tesla placed a $685 million actuator order with Chinese supplier Sanhua Intelligent Control in October 2025, consistent with Sanhua being a likely Optimus actuator supplier building on its existing Tesla thermal-management relationship (Model 3/X/S since 2017, over 35% global market share in thermal components).
evidence.source_name: 36Kr, Tesla-Sanhua actuator order article

evidence.claim: Precision-component maker Taoshi has already secured a supply agreement for 100,000 units of joint modules specifically for dexterous hands, i.e. actuator/joint modules are a direct input into hand assembly.
evidence.source_name: 36Kr, Taoshi Intelligent Technology financing and capacity article

evidence.claim: Sanhua's actuator assemblies, won via a $685 million order, are being supplied directly into Tesla's Optimus OEM humanoid platform.
evidence.source_name: 36Kr, Tesla-Sanhua actuator order article

evidence.claim: Schaeffler's co-developed strain-wave actuators are being supplied into OEM humanoid platforms under partnerships with Neura Robotics, Humanoid, and Leju Robotics.
evidence.source_name: KraneShares, "Humanoid Robotics In 2026: The Race From Pilot To Platform"

links.name: Dexterous hands
links.role: The single most cost-driving hardware element in a humanoid: the most sophisticated models offer roughly 24 degrees of freedom and cost more than $70,000 each, which is why hand cost reduction gates the economics of any high-volume deployment [Fraunhofer IPA humanoid hardware value chain, as of 2026-02].

bottleneck.note: Cost, not supply, is the constraint here; almost all specialists are private, so listed exposure is via their actuator and sensor suppliers rather than the hand makers.

evidence.claim: The dexterous-hand market has cycled through degrees-of-freedom competition (20 DOF, 24 DOF, 30+ DOF models), with cost pressure from thousands of tactile contact points and expensive high-pixel electronic skin per hand; the industry is now shifting from DOF-spec competition toward real-world implementation capability.
evidence.source_name: 36Kr, dexterous-hand degrees-of-freedom competition article

evidence.claim: Dexterous-hand degrees-of-freedom and design competition is explicitly framed as driven by humanoid OEMs selecting hand specs for their own platforms, i.e. dexterous hands are a component selected and integrated by the OEM into its finished robot.
evidence.source_name: 36Kr, dexterous-hand degrees-of-freedom competition article

links.name: Humanoid OEMs & platform integrators
links.role: The layer retail already owns: Tesla runs 1,000+ Optimus Gen 3 units internally, Unitree shipped roughly 5,500 units in 2025 (the highest volume of any producer), and Figure, Apptronik and Agility are in paid industrial deployment; platforms lean on vertical integration and dedicated plants to cut unit cost [HumanoidApplications / Technology.org deployment tracking, as of 2026-07].

bottleneck.note: Not a bottleneck and not un-crowded: this is the retail story the signal is deliberately looking past. Most credible volume producers (Figure, Unitree, Apptronik, Agility, 1X) are private.

evidence.claim: Unitree Robotics shipped approximately 5,500 humanoid units across its product line in 2025, surpassing Figure's total historical output, with plans to reach 10,000 units in subsequent years.
evidence.source_name: Technology.org, "Humanoid Robots in 2026: What Is Actually Deployed"

evidence.claim: Elon Musk confirmed in January 2026 that over 1,000 Optimus Gen 3 robots were operating on Tesla's Fremont production floor, deployed on live lines building customer vehicles, with zero external unit sales as of that date.
evidence.source_name: iFactoryApp, "Tesla Optimus at Fremont: Gen 3 Humanoid 2026" (relaying a Musk statement)

evidence.claim: Figure, Agility, and Apptronik are described as building purpose-built industrial humanoid robots for narrow tasks, as opposed to Unitree's cost/volume strategy, i.e. the OEM's finished robot is the input to paid industrial deployment.
evidence.source_name: Technology.org, "Humanoid Robots in 2026: What Is Actually Deployed"

links.name: Deployment & end customers
links.role: Where units are actually earning: Figure humanoids have contributed to production of 30,000+ vehicles at BMW Spartanburg on ten-hour shifts five days a week, with Agility's Digit at Amazon and Toyota and Apptronik's Apollo at Mercedes — the proof the pilot-to-volume crossing is real rather than promised [HumanoidApplications / Technology.org deployment tracking, as of 2026-07].

bottleneck.note: Demand is the validation signal, not the constraint; exposure here is diluted inside very large industrial buyers and is not an investable expression of this chain.

evidence.claim: Figure's F.02 humanoid robot contributed to the production of over 30,000 BMW X3 vehicles at the Spartanburg plant, running ten-hour shifts Monday through Friday, logging over 1,250 runtime hours and loading over 90,000 parts, scaling from initial operation to full production-line integration within 10 months.
evidence.source_name: Figure AI, "F.02 Contributed to the Production of 30,000 Cars at BMW"

evidence.claim: Agility Robotics' Digit humanoid is in commercial Robots-as-a-Service deployment with Toyota Motor Manufacturing Canada following a successful pilot; the announcement states Toyota joins other Fortune 500 companies using Digit, including GXO, Schaeffler, and Amazon.
evidence.source_name: Agility Robotics, "Agility Robotics Announces Commercial Agreement with Toyota Motor Manufacturing Canada"

evidence.claim: Apptronik and Mercedes-Benz entered a commercial agreement described as Apptronik's first publicly announced commercial deployment of its Apollo humanoid and the first application of humanoid robotics at Mercedes-Benz.
evidence.source_name: Apptronik, "Apptronik and Mercedes-Benz Enter Commercial Agreement"

changelog.change: chain built from SIG-20260829-03 via Run-button click (queue id q-1788027370056): 13 links from NdFeB magnets through precision machine tools, the reducer/screw/motor tier, integrated actuators, hands, power and compute, to OEMs and deployment; every link role carries a cited dated source, heat unscored

renumbered upstream-first per method 4 (amended 2026-08-29): position 1 is now the furthest-upstream link, the last position is the demand anchor. 10 of 13 links moved. Topological order computed from the existing edges, so the map's structure is unchanged and nothing analytical moved.

citation backfill (method 4): added dated evidence[] to all 13 links and all 16 edges (each edge cited via an evidence item on its upstream link with supports naming the downstream link id). Sources are company primary announcements (Figure AI, Agility Robotics, Apptronik, Nabtesco, Harmonic Drive Systems) and specialist humanoid-supply-chain research (36Kr, humanoid.guide, TechBuzzChina, KraneShares, WhyChips, Adamas Intelligence, Humanoids Daily, China Unread, DataM Intelligence, arXiv, Technology.org). All tagged INFERRED: none of the named suppliers (Figure AI, Agility, Apptronik, Nabtesco, Harmonic Drive Systems, Leaderdrive, Sanhua, Schaeffler subsidiaries named) file with the SEC, so method 4's VERIFIED bar (SEC-registrant filing) does not apply to this chain; every item still carries a dated, fetchable, real URL. Two sources named in the original inline citations could not be verified and were dropped rather than guessed: no real 'Vicon' humanoid-market report exists (only an unrelated motion-capture company), and no dated source paired the Fraunhofer-cited '~24 DOF' figure with the '>$70,000' dexterous-hand price point; both links still carry other, verified citations. No heat, scenario, structure, or score field touched.
